newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares retreat at the close, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares retreat at the close, end lower.

text.p: Chilean shares, still reeling from poor third-quarter earnings reports, closed slightly lower after a late wave of bargain-hunting petered out, traders said.
But brokers said the market had climbed from support levels and could see some rises in the next session, with many stocks now considered cheap, they said.
"The bolsa has touched bottom and should rise gently for the next few sessions," said one trader.
The 40-share IPSA index ended 0.07 percent lower at 97.73 points. The general IGPA index ended 0.09 percent lower at 5347.24 points amid light volume of 7.9 billion pesos traded.
Wall Street's post-election surge had little impact on local stocks which continue hit by poorer-than-expected company nine-month earnings, said traders.
Electricity stocks were hurt by fears that cuts in generating and distribution rates will have a serious impact on company earnings, they said.

The government has announced a cut of about 11 percent in generating prices and was expected to release new distribution rates Wednesday afternoon. These are widely forecast to fall by around 10 percent.
Endesa closed down 0.2 percent at 252-1/2 pesos with Enersis off 0.1 percent at 242-1/2 pesos.
Gainers included companies which reported strong earnings, including drug-maker LabChile, up 2.39 percent at 343 pesos, and winery Concha y Toro, which firmed 3.99 percent to 169-1/2 pesos.
Manufacturing firm Masisa rose 4.2 percent to 198 pesos.
